issues.legal_issue: Whether land assessed for agricultural purposes when let qualifies as premises for an application to fix standard rent, despite a later change in its permitted use.
material_facts: The land was assessed for agricultural purposes when it was let and remained so assessed until the Collector later permitted its conversion to non-agricultural use.
The leases allowed buildings to be constructed after obtaining approval, but no such conversion had been permitted when the land was let.
After the conversion was permitted, the tenant applied to fix standard rent under the rent-control statute.
issues.conclusion: The land was not premises under the statute when it was let, and the later conversion did not make the standard-rent application maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(8) and 6(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging Houses Rates Control Act, 1947, the relevant status of land as premises is determined at the date of letting. Land assessed for agricultural purposes does not become non-agricultural merely because it lies fallow; under section 65 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879, its use could be changed by an order of the Collector. Section 11 therefore did not permit standard rent to be fixed for land that was not premises at the date of letting. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.standard_rent_fixation_proceeding: A tenant applies to a court to fix the rent of land under a rent-control regime.
predicates.land_assessed_for_agriculture_at_letting: The land was assessed for agricultural purposes when it was let.

issues.definition: When a tenant applies to fix rent under a rent-control regime for land assessed for agricultural purposes at the time it was let, the application is not maintainable.
